component_findings.async_structured: Recertified level 4 under the current criterion: Asynchronous concurrency has first-class composition and structured lifetime/join/cancellation mechanisms or an equivalent disciplined model. Evidence basis: Java | Java concurrency is now among the strongest in the fixed language set: virtual threads give Go-goroutine-like ergonomics while retaining a best-in-class concurrent library and rigorously specified memory model; lacks Rust's compile-time race freedom. | java.util.concurrent: mature library of thread pools (ExecutorService), concurrent collections (ConcurrentHashMap), synchronizers (CountDownLatch, Semaphore, CyclicBarrier), atomics, and locks (ReentrantLock, StampedLock) | Virtual threads (Project Loom, JEP 444, finalized JDK 21): lightweight JVM-managed user-mode threads scaling blocking code to millions of concurrent tasks without separate async/await syntax | Structured concurrency (JEP 480, preview) formalizes parent/child task lifetime and error propagation | java.util.concurrent.Flow and CompletableFuture give composable async pipelines | Memory model (JLS Chapter 17) is a well-specified happens-before model | synchronized keyword and monitor-based intrinsic locks as a simple built-in primitive | JEP 444 (virtual threads), JEP 480 (structured concurrency), java.util.concurrent design, JLS Chapter 17 memory model; design-level assessment. | No compile-time data-race prevention comparable to Rust ownership/borrow checker and Send/Sync traits | Historical thread-per-request model was expensive before virtual threads (now mitigated) | No native async/await syntax; pre-L…

metric.concurrency.limitations: Comparison-language reprojection requires the preserved paid source evidence plus the historical program/workload/toolchain inputs to match the current shard; mismatches remain misses.
metric.concurrency.selection_rule: Judge intrinsic concurrency/parallelism semantics and core runtime primitives. External frameworks and debugger/tool maturity are out of scope.

component_findings.abi_calling_control: Recertified level 3 under the current criterion: ABI/calling-convention/linkage choices are explicit or safely standardized for common interoperability cases. Evidence basis: Java | Materially better than the legacy JNI baseline, but behind C/Rust/Zig zero-overhead direct ABI interop, roughly comparable to or slightly behind Swift/Kotlin given JVM boundary overhead and manual layout descriptors. | Java Foreign Function & Memory (FFM) API (JEP 454, finalized JDK 22), preceded by JNI for two decades | JDK 22 FFM API (JEP 454) and java.lang.foreign package design knowledge; design-level metric, no execution required. | FFM API provides safe, arena-scoped native memory management (MemorySegment, Arena) without hand-written glue/native code, unlike JNI | Method handles + linker (Linker.nativeLinker()) allow calling C functions directly from pure Java via FunctionDescriptor, no C stubs required for simple calls | Confinement model ties native memory lifetime to Java thread/arena scope, giving compile-time-adjacent safety over manual malloc/free | jextract tool can auto-generate Java bindings from C headers, reducing boilerplate | Bidirectional interop: Java can expose upcalls via Linker.upcallStub | Legacy JNI (still widely used) requires hand-written C glue code and manual reference management, heavier than Rust extern C or Go cgo | FFM API still requires explicit layout descriptors mirroring C struct layouts by hand for complex structs; no automatic ABI struct derivation like Rust bindgen or C# P/Invoke source generators | No language-native unsafe-bloc…
